<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_shape (literal, a string literal in datasetQueryBodyRefusal), unknown_field (literal, a string literal in datasetQueryBodyRefusal))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`  _(via datasetName (literal, a string literal in DATASET_QUERY_BODY_KEYS; a string literal in datasetQueryBodyRefusal), previewDrafts (literal, a string literal in DATASET_QUERY_BODY_KEYS), runtimeFilter (literal, a string literal in remedyFor), selection.runtimeFilter (literal, a string literal in remedyFor))_
- `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`  _(via runtimeFilter (literal, a string literal in remedyFor))_
- `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx`  _(via runtimeFilter (literal, a string literal in remedyFor))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via runtimeFilter (literal, a string literal in remedyFor))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via unknown_field (literal, a string literal in datasetQueryBodyRefusal))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via runtimeFilter (literal, a string literal in remedyFor))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via runtimeFilter (literal, a string literal in remedyFor))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via invalid_shape (literal, a string literal in datasetQueryBodyRefusal))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via runtimeFilter (literal, a string literal in remedyFor))_
- `content/docs/releases/v9.mdx`  _(via runtimeFilter (literal, a string literal in remedyFor))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 39 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6a04e3af7756446bb7a2e73973f09e011090312` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c7842c2ce05d9395a760aeaedb1095fc6ad75dfe` — the merge of head `9b9d5b7b04d69e7dc908254deca27529d35a5b9d` into base `f6a04e3af7756446bb7a2e73973f09e011090312`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c7842c2ce05d9395a760aeaedb1095fc6ad75dfe && git checkout c7842c2ce05d9395a760aeaedb1095fc6ad75dfe
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f6a04e3af7756446bb7a2e73973f09e011090312 9b9d5b7b04d69e7dc908254deca27529d35a5b9d && git checkout -B drift-repro f6a04e3af7756446bb7a2e73973f09e011090312 && git merge --no-ff 9b9d5b7b04d69e7dc908254deca27529d35a5b9d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6a04e3af7756446bb7a2e73973f09e011090312
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f6a04e3af7756446bb7a2e73973f09e011090312` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dbf091e2099bbdbc43dd738199f50dd7fe6d9035`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-body-door.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-body-door.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/analytics-dataset-body-door.dogfood.test.ts + packages/rest/src/analytics-selection-door.ts, packages/spec/src/api/analytics.zod.ts (DatasetSelectionSchema, its aliases and guidance), packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts and lazy-schema.ts (whether `.shape` is reachable through the lazy proxy), packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts (the sibling `/analytics/query` envelope, `errorResponseBase`), packages/runtime/src/domains/analytics.ts (`assertAnalyticsQueryBody`), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (the ADR-0114 field-code vocabulary), packages/client/src/index.ts (`analytics.queryDataset`), ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts (`queryDataset`, `readAnalyticsErrorEnvelope`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/DatasetPreview.tsx, packages/verify/src/dashboard-window.ts, the ten existing dogfood suites that post to this door, content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx. The face is the narrowing face: `--template --paths` on the PR's file list names no `hits` and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line, so the floor is every diff path outside the prose faces (the four code and test paths above); the changeset and the doc page are the lane seat's ACCEPT and were read, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set change at `POST {basePath}/analytics/dataset/query` (both the plain and the `/environments/:environmentId` mount): the body's top-level key set closes to `dataset`, `datasetName`, `previewDrafts`, `selection`. Right.** Read on the head's `analytics-routes.ts`: the handler reads exactly `body.selection`, `body.previewDrafts`, `body.dataset` and `body.datasetName`, and the only thing passed on is `svc.queryDataset(dataset, selection, context, previewDrafts ? { previewDrafts: true } : undefined)`: no other body member reaches the analytics service, the metadata lookup (`getMetaItems({ type: 'dataset', previewDrafts })`) or the `DatasetSchema` parse. `DATASET_QUERY_BODY_KEYS` equals the read set, and nothing is stripped or rewritten (the door returns a refusal or `undefined`; `body` reaches the handler as sent).
2. **A fifth key answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, flat `{ code, message, details: { fields: [{ field, code: 'unknown_field', message }] } }`, and the query does not run. Right, and the frame is the right one.** `unknown_field` and `invalid_shape` are both in the ADR-0114 vocabulary (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`, lines 248-249; `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` lists them). The envelope is the frame this door already answers with everywhere: the `selection` refusal (`analytics-selection-door.ts`: `{ code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED', message, details: { fields } }`), the inline `selection.measures` 400, the "Provide body.dataset" 400 and the "Invalid dataset definition." 400 are all flat. The sibling `/analytics/query` is a dispatcher route and answers through `errorResponseBase` as `{ success: false, error: { code, message, details } }`; the only thing the dev borrowed from it is the sentence opening (`Unrecognized key(s) on this dataset query: …`, the strictObject surface phrasing). A nested frame here would have been the first nested refusal on a door whose five other refusals are flat, and `@objectstack/client.analytics.queryDataset` is documented as the one analytics method with no envelope (#12104 / #13079). The console's `readAnalyticsErrorEnvelope` reads both the flat and the wrapped frame, so the refusal's code and sentence reach the dashboard banner either way. The deviation is correct.
3. **Remedy derivation. Right.** `runtimeFilter` and the three filter near-misses (`filter`, `filters`, `where`) say `selection.runtimeFilter`; any other key in `DatasetSelectionSchema.shape` says `selection.KEY`. `.shape` is reachable: `lazySchema` is a Proxy whose `get` forwards every non-`_zod` property to the resolved real schema, and `strictObject` returns `closedObject(z.object(shape, …).strict())`, whose constructor calls `ZodObject.init`, so `.shape` is the declared member map (`dimensions`, `measures`, `runtimeFilter`, `timeDimensions`, `dateGranularity`, `order`, `limit`, `offset`, `compareTo`, `totals`, `timezone`). The rest pin's "misplaced `dimensions`" case exercises that path through the real route. The three near-miss spellings are exactly the three the spec curates as `runtimeFilter` aliases one level down (`analytics.zod.ts` lines 632-634), so the two levels agree today.
4. **`dataset` beside `datasetName` answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming both (`invalid_shape`), before any lookup or query. Right on the ambiguity, with one edge that is wider than the changeset states (see ④, should-fix).** Before: the handler's `let dataset = body.dataset; if (!dataset && body.datasetName) …` ran the inline definition and dropped the name silently. The census (re-run, item 6) found no producer sending both, so the delta's acceptance 3 says refuse it in this PR, and it does.
5. **No published surface moves.** `datasetQueryBodyRefusal` and `DATASET_QUERY_BODY_KEYS` are new exports of a module `packages/rest/src/index.ts` does not re-export (same posture as `analytics-selection-door.ts`); no `packages/spec` edit, no `ui/` edit, no `@objectstack/client` signature change. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right declaration; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (nothing an author writes in metadata changes).
6. **Producer census, re-run independently on the head tree. The dev's table holds.** `@objectstack/client.analytics.queryDataset` (packages/client/src/index.ts:2548) is typed `{ dataset?, datasetName?, selection, previewDrafts? }` and posts the payload as given. The console adapter (`ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` ~7164) builds the body as a ternary, `{ datasetName, selection, previewDrafts?: true }` or `{ dataset, selection, previewDrafts?: true }`, never both, never a fifth key; `DatasetPreview.tsx` goes through that adapter. `@objectstack/verify` `dashboard-window.ts:773` sends `{ datasetName, selection }`. The ten existing dogfood suites send `dataset` or `datasetName`, `selection`, with `runtimeFilter` only inside `selection`. The docs example (`analytics.mdx` lines 259-263) sends `{ datasetName, selection }`; `data-api.mdx`, `cli.mdx`, `services-checklist.mdx` and the generated `references/api/analytics.mdx` only name the route. MCP (`packages/mcp`), `service-ai`, the CLI, `packages/plugins` and `apps/**` have no caller of this door. No producer sends a key outside the four, and none sends both `dataset` and `datasetName`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29156-dataset-query-body-unknown-keys.md`: `@objectstack/rest` **patch**, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on line-initial positions, a **BREAKING** banner with Before / Now / Unchanged / Who sees it bullets and the remedy, and exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker (a category `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` lists). That is the level AGENTS.md Post-Task item 3 prescribes under ruling A (#25105): the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition." The PR title carries the `!`, and the PR body's two declaration lines match the changeset's. `Check Changeset` on this head is green (completed · success). The disposition is right: the refusal names each key and where it belongs, so a migration would have nothing to rewrite. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Claim amendment (`Clause-②: no` → `no (narrowing)`).** Right: the diff refuses bodies that answered 200, which is a narrowing on a REST data door; the claim amendment 6574727839 aligns the claim with the PR and changeset. Nothing further.
- **Envelope deviation (flat frame, not the dispatcher's nested one).** Answered in ① item 2: the flat frame is the only consistent choice on this door; the delta's "in the sibling door's frame" is satisfied by the sentence opening, and the nesting would have split one door into two dialects. Accepted.
- **PR attribution (assignee / reviewer via MCP not set).** Not a contract matter; the standard order forbids MCP writes, so the omission is correct. No action.
- **Open question: rest-side near-miss table (A) vs exporting spec's alias map (B).** A. The three spellings answer a misplaced key one level up, which is this door's own remedy, not the spec's unknown-key suggester; exporting the alias map would be a new public export of `@objectstack/spec` (`Clause-②: yes`, a spec card) in exchange for three strings that the spec's own alias block already pins by name. If the spec grows a fourth alias for `runtimeFilter`, the rest table will lag by one word, which is a prose-level drift, not a silent widening. Keep A; B only if a third surface starts reading the aliases.
- **Out-of-scope note (the route's query string is not a closed set; only `?preview` multiplicity is judged).** Correctly left out: the card is the body, and the query-string allowlist is converted per lane under the ingress policy. Noted, not escalated.
- **Author:** PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no second author to name.
- **CI at review time:** `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links` are green; `Test Core (1-8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Live E2E UI` were still in progress. This verdict is on the diff; the all-green landing gate is the seat's check before queueing.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-body-door.ts` and `analytics-routes.ts`: the narrowing holds.**

- **Refusal before any query runs.** The door is called right after `const body = req.body ?? {}`, after `enforceAuth` and the 501 service check (so an unauthenticated or service-less caller keeps its earlier answer, as before) and before the `selection.measures` check, `datasetSelectionRefusal`, `refuseRepeatedQueryParams`, the `previewDrafts` read, the `getMetaItems` lookup, the `DatasetSchema` parse and `queryDataset`. Both refusals return before `getMetaItems` and `queryDataset`; the rest pin asserts `queryDataset` was never called on every refusal and `getMetaItems` was never called on the ambiguous body. The dogfood pin proves it over HTTP on the showcase (400 with the remedy where `selection.runtimeFilter` on the same stack answers 0).
- **Valid bodies byte-unchanged.** The door is validation-only: it returns `undefined` or a refusal, never a parsed object, and the handler keeps reading `body.selection`, `body.previewDrafts`, `body.dataset`, `body.datasetName` off the same object. A non-object body (array, string, null) passes the door as `undefined` and lands in the pre-existing `selection.measures` 400, as before. The §3 controls assert the service receives the caller's `selection` (with `runtimeFilter` intact) and the resolved dataset, and that the selection-level refusal and the "Provide body.dataset" sentence are unchanged.
- **`previewDrafts` semantics unchanged.** The key is in the closed set; its read (`body.previewDrafts === true || req.query?.preview === 'draft'`, gated by `mayReadPendingDrafts(context)`) is untouched and still sits after the door, so the `?preview=draft` query-string path and the draft-read admission are as they were. The value is not judged (a `previewDrafts: 'yes'` is still ignored as not-`true`), which is the pre-existing behaviour and outside this card.
- **The remedy cannot point at a dead key.** `remedyFor` reads `DatasetSelectionSchema.shape`, which holds only the members the selection accepts; the spec's `guidance` block already tells a caller who puts `dataset`, `datasetName` or `previewDrafts` inside `selection` to move them up, so the two doors now describe one body shape from both sides.
- **Message determinism.** Unknown keys are sorted before the sentence and the `fields[]` are built, so a multi-key refusal reads the same whatever order the adapter built the object in (pinned).

**Should-fix (not a FAIL):**

1. **The ambiguity test is wider than the handler's old branch by one degenerate body.** `datasetQueryBodyRefusal` treats `datasetName` as supplied when it is `!== undefined && !== null`, while the handler's branch it replaces (`if (!dataset && body.datasetName)`) treats a falsy name (`''`, `0`, `false`) as absent. So `{ dataset: {...}, datasetName: '' }` ran the inline definition before and answers 400 now, one body more than the changeset's "Before" bullet describes ("`dataset` beside `datasetName` ran the inline definition"). No producer sends it (the console's ternary never emits a name beside `dataset`; the client passes the caller's payload through), so it changes no real caller, but the refusal set and the handler's own notion of "a name was supplied" should be one test. Either read `record.datasetName` by the handler's truthiness (then `{ dataset, datasetName: '' }` keeps running inline and the "Before" bullet is exact) or say in the changeset that an empty-string name beside `dataset` is now refused too. A follow-up commit on this PR, or a note, is enough.
2. **The near-miss table and the spec's alias block are two copies of three words.** Accepted as A in ③; a one-line comment in `analytics.zod.ts` beside the `where / filter / filters` aliases naming `analytics-dataset-body-door.ts` as the other reader would make the next spec edit find the rest table. Not required for this PR (no `packages/spec` edit on this card).

Nothing here takes a declared capability away from a consumer: every body the census found a producer sending is served as before and reaches the service with the same arguments, and the only bodies refused are ones the spec's own `DatasetSelectionSchema` guidance already describes as misplaced.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-9bs2fu`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmQxwoGb5fSnrFkpxmt`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9b9d5b7b04d69e7dc908254deca27529d35a5b9d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-body-door.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-body-door.test.ts (the two paths the delta moves), packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/analytics-dataset-body-door.dogfood.test.ts (byte-identical to the reviewed head, per the delta's diff-stat) + packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts (the handler branch the new condition cites, `let dataset = body.dataset; if (!dataset && body.datasetName)`), .changeset/29156-dataset-query-body-unknown-keys.md and content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx (prose faces, read for whether the Before bullet is now exact), the ten dogfood suites that post to this door (read for a body carrying both keys or a falsy name), the PR body as it stands.

This is the delta re-review of the findings-only commit on top of the full review at `dbf091e2` (record comment 6574905951, PASS, should-fix 1). The new head is one commit, a fast-forward of `dbf091e2` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` holds), and `git diff dbf091e2..9b9d5b7b` touches 2 files, 18 insertions and 5 deletions: the door module's doc comment, the one ambiguity condition, and two pins. Judged on that diff, not on the dev's account of it.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The ambiguity condition is now exactly the handler's truthiness on both keys. Right.** The door reads `if (record.dataset && record.datasetName)`, where `record` is the same `body` object (`req.body ?? {}`) the handler then reads, cast and not copied. The handler's branch is `let dataset = body.dataset; if (!dataset && body.datasetName) { ...saved lookup... }`: a truthy `dataset` wins, a falsy `dataset` beside a truthy `datasetName` runs the saved definition, and both falsy falls to the pre-existing "Provide body.dataset" 400. The door's refusal fires only in the one cell the handler never distinguished (both truthy), and passes every other cell through to the handler unchanged: `{ dataset: {...}, datasetName: '' | 0 | false | null | absent }` runs inline, `{ dataset: null | undefined | false, datasetName: 'x' }` runs the saved dataset. The reviewed head's `!== undefined && !== null` refused `{ dataset, datasetName: '' }` (and `0`, `false`), one cell wider than the handler; that cell is the whole behavioural delta between `dbf091e2` and `9b9d5b7b`, and it moves back to the pre-PR answer (200, inline). Should-fix 1 of the full record is closed by its first option.
2. **Nothing else moves.** The unknown-key branch, `DATASET_QUERY_BODY_KEYS`, the remedy table, the sorted `fields[]`, the flat `{ code, message, details: { fields } }` envelope on both refusals, the `invalid_shape` and `unknown_field` codes, the two messages and the call site in `analytics-routes.ts` are byte-identical to `dbf091e2`. The changeset and the doc page are untouched by the delta; the changeset's Before bullet ("A body naming both `dataset` and `datasetName` ran the inline definition and dropped the name without a word") is now exact rather than one body narrow, and its Unchanged bullet (`null` `dataset` beside a name still runs the saved dataset) still holds. No published surface moves: no `packages/spec`, no `ui/`, no `@objectstack/client` edit; the module is still not re-exported from `packages/rest/src/index.ts`.
3. **The pins pin it.** The new loop posts `{ dataset: inlineDataset, datasetName, selection }` for `datasetName` in `''` and `null` through the real route and asserts 200, `queryDataset` called once with the inline measures (`revenue`), and `getMetaItems` never called. Under the reviewed head's condition the `''` case answers 400 (`'' !== undefined && '' !== null`), so that pin reds on exactly the cell the delta changes; the `null` case was already green under the old condition and guards the other spelling of "absent" against a future presence check (`'datasetName' in record`). The existing "both supplied" refusal pin (truthy name) and the `null`-`dataset` control still stand, so the three cells of the truthiness table are each pinned from the inside. File count: 16 `it(` lines, two loops (3 near-miss keys, 2 falsy names) → 19 cases, matching the body's "19 of 19". The dev's ablation reading (old condition back: 1 failed, 18 passed) is consistent with this reading; not re-run here.
4. **Not re-running the dogfood battery is acceptable for this delta.** The only body whose answer differs between `dbf091e2` and `9b9d5b7b` is a truthy `dataset` beside a falsy-but-present `datasetName`. Read on the head tree: the four cases in `analytics-dataset-body-door.dogfood.test.ts` send `datasetName` alone; `analytics-inline-dataset-isolation` and `analytics-inline-dataset-admission` are the only dogfood files naming both keys, and each does so in separate bodies (`saved` reads with `datasetName` alone, the probes and refusals with `dataset` alone); the other seven suites send one key each. No dogfood body sends both keys and none sends `datasetName: ''`, `0`, `false` or `null` (grep over `packages/qa/dogfood`, `packages/rest/src`, `packages/verify`, `ui/packages/data-objectstack`, `packages/client/src`: no hit). The full-battery reading at `dbf091e2` therefore covers this head for every body it exercises; `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green on `9b9d5b7b` as well.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged by the delta and still right: `@objectstack/rest` patch, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in the changeset and the PR body, BREAKING banner, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. The delta narrows nothing further; it gives back one degenerate body the reviewed head had over-refused, so the declared narrowing is now no wider than the changeset states. `Check Changeset` on `9b9d5b7b`: one completed run success, a second run in progress at read time.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Should-fix 1 of record 6574905951 (over-refusal of `{ dataset, datasetName: '' }`).** Closed by the delta, option one (handler truthiness), with pins. Nothing further.
